solution: Take natural logarithms: $x\\ln2+y\\ln3=\\ln12=\\ln(4\\cdot3)=2\\ln2+\\ln3$, and $x\\ln3+y\\ln2=\\ln18=\\ln(9\\cdot2)=2\\ln3+\\ln2$. Adding these two equations gives $(x+y)(\\ln2+\\ln3)=3(\\ln2+\\ln3)$, so $x+y=3$. Subtracting gives $(x-y)(\\ln2-\\ln3)=\\ln2-\\ln3$, so $x-y=1$. Solving yields $x=2$ and $y=1$. (Check: $2^{2}3^{1}=12$ and $3^{2}2^{1}=18$, both satisfied.)
hints: Add and subtract the two log equations.
Solve the resulting linear system for x+y and x-y.
